title: How a convection current warms a whole room
examples: Why are heaters placed low and air conditioners high?

explain.say: Here is a puzzle. A heater sits low near the floor, but an air conditioner is fixed high on the wall. Is that a mistake? Not at all! Both use convection, which means heat carried by a moving liquid or gas. Let us follow the air.

explain.say: Look at the first stage. Air next to the heater warms up. Its particles move faster and spread out. Spread-out air is less dense, which means lighter for its size. So look at the second stage: the warm air floats up. Which way does it go?

explain.say: Up, yes! At the ceiling it spreads across the room, then cools down. See the fourth stage? Cool air is denser, so it sinks back down. Then it flows along the floor to the heater to be warmed again. Can you see the loop?

explain.say: That loop is a convection current. It keeps carrying warmth all around the room. Now the air conditioner: it sends cold air out high up, and cold air sinks, so it spreads down through the whole room. Smart, right?

explain.say: Excellent thinking! Wow fact: huge convection currents in Earth's air make winds and sea breezes, and slow convection deep inside the Earth moves whole continents a few centimetres a year. Challenge: watch the steam above a hot cup of tea. Which way does it swirl?

faq.a: A convection current is a loop of moving liquid or gas: warm fluid rises, cools, sinks and is warmed again.
Heating makes air particles spread out, so the air becomes less dense than the cooler air around it and floats upwards.
asks: Why does warm air go up?

faq.q: Why can convection not happen in solids?
faq.a: Particles in a solid cannot flow from place to place, so heat cannot be carried by moving fluid. Solids use conduction instead.

faq.q: Why are air conditioners placed high on the wall?
faq.a: Cold air is denser and sinks, so releasing it high lets it fall and spread through the whole room.
asks: Why is the AC mounted high?

faq.a: In a pan of boiling water, in sea and land breezes, in weather systems and in the slow movement of rock deep inside the Earth.

facts: Convection happens in liquids and gases (fluids), not in solids.
Warm fluids rise because they are less dense than the cooler fluid around them.

quiz.why: Warm air expands, becomes less dense and is pushed up by the denser cool air around it.

wrong.0: Heavier, denser air sinks, not rises.
wrong.2: Nothing pulls it; it floats up because it is less dense.

quiz.why: Convection needs a fluid that can flow, so liquids and gases.

wrong.0: Solid particles cannot flow, so convection cannot happen in them.
wrong.1: Convection needs moving particles; space has almost none.
